title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Over a base ring A (Z, Z_l or Z-hat), Grothendieck studies 'loop equations' in GL(2,A) built from the two torsion generators of SL(2,Z): rho of order 6 and sigma = sigma_infty = [[0,-1],[1,0]] of order 4. Recall SL(2,Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6. These are linear (GL_2) shadows of the twisted-conjugation equations of the Teichmüller/GT theory in the 'Longue Marche' continuation. The equation is: given eta in GL(2,A), find beta with eta = beta sigma beta^{-1} sigma^{-1} = [beta, sigma] (27). The commutator form is clearly intended; the written 'beta sigma (beta)^{-1}' is a slip.

Step 1 (necessary conditions). From (27), eta sigma = beta sigma beta^{-1} is conjugate to sigma. Hence det eta = 1 and Tr(eta sigma) = Tr sigma = 0 (28). Computing eta sigma = [[S,-R],[U,-T]] turns (28) into RU - ST = 1 and S = T (29). So eta must be symmetric of determinant 1.

Step 2 (local-global / class group). If eta sigma is conjugate to sigma locally, global conjugacy in GL(2,Z) is governed by ideal classes of A_sigma = Z[sigma] = Z[i], by Latimer–MacDuffee. On the previous page Grothendieck records Pic(A_sigma) = 1. So a beta in GL(2,Z) exists. The remaining obstruction to choosing beta in SL(2,Z), i.e. controlling the sign of det beta, lies in Z^*/N(A_sigma^*) = {±1}/{1} = ±1.

Step 3 (formula (31)). With beta = [[r,s],[t,u]] and delta = det beta, one computes beta sigma beta^{-1} = (1/delta)[[rt+su, -(r^2+s^2)], [t^2+u^2, -(ut+rs)]]. The (2,1) entry gives delta·U = t^2 + u^2 = N(t sigma + u). Hence sign(det beta) = sign(U). Equivalently, sigma g^{-1} sigma^{-1} = det(g)^{-1} g^T, so:
- if det beta = 1, then eta = beta beta^T is positive definite;
- if det beta = -1, then eta = -beta beta^T is negative definite.
Since RU = 1 + S^2 > 0, a symmetric unimodular eta is always definite. Solvability of (27) then amounts to eta being ± a form equivalent to x^2+y^2, which holds because the class number of discriminant -4 is 1. The sign in SL(2) is read off from U.

The next page summarises this (together with the rho analogue) as a Proposition. It adds that the l-adic / Z-hat obstruction is detected by U mod 4.
errors: (27) as written, 'beta sigma (beta)^{-1}', omits the final sigma^{-1}. It must be the commutator beta sigma beta^{-1} sigma^{-1}, as the bracket notation and the subsequent computation require.
(31) reads '(rt - su) U = t^2+u^2'. The correct factor is det beta = ru - st; this is either a slip of the pen or a misreading.
The page asserts a solution beta in GL(2,Z) exists given (29) plus local solvability. This is correct (class number 1 of Z[i]), but the local hypothesis is not verified on this page.

ideas.what: Commutator/twisted-conjugacy equation [beta, sigma] = eta in GL_2 with sigma of order 4; necessary conditions det = 1 and eta symmetric
ideas.modern_name: Conjugacy of a matrix to sigma; eta = ±beta beta^T (symmetric unimodular forms)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Gauss reduction of binary quadratic forms)

ideas.what: Global conjugacy of matrices with characteristic polynomial x^2+1 governed by Pic(Z[i]) = 1, with SL vs GL obstruction in Z^*/N(A_sigma^*)
ideas.modern_name: Latimer–MacDuffee–Taussky correspondence; norm-residue obstruction for SL-conjugacy

ideas.what: Linearised (GL_2) version of the loop equations attached to the order-4 and order-6 generators of SL(2,Z), as a test case for the Teichmüller/GT program
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck program; Drinfeld, Ihara for GT
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the SL(2,Z) / Teichmüller tower generally, not these computations

deep.surprise_reason: A correct but elementary computation: commutator equation with the order-4 element of SL(2,Z), reduced to classical facts about Z[i] and binary forms of discriminant -4. Interesting only as context for Grothendieck's linear test cases of the loop equations; nothing new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'de F_sigma (en plus de la condition de régularité ... eta sigma)'. The underlined word is likely 'singularité' / 'régularité' of eta sigma, matching the next page's 'soit singulière'.

'(as [?])' is likely '(cas où la base est Z)'. The passage reads roughly: 'il s'ensuit (cas où la base est Z) que l'on peut trouver une solution beta (∈ GL(2,Z)) de (27); l'obstruction pour trouver une solution dans SL(2,Z) et non seulement GL(2,Z) se trouve dans Z^*/N(A_sigma^*) ≃ ±1'.
(31): the image reads '(rt - su) U'; mathematically this should be (ru - st) U.
'c'est que [?] soit' is probably 'c'est que l'on ait' or 'c'est-à-dire soit'.
